new.v: $10,000 in gold and a gold watch (story)
new.tovw: Lead grade F: the gold was dug up and recovered by the neighbours in January 1901 and passed to the heir; nothing reported left.
new.n: Israel Noel's $10,000 in gold, dug from his cellar by neighbours, Fayette (found 1901)
new.pl: Israel Noel's house at Fayette, Lafayette County; lot not yet found (ring 3 km on the village)
new.st: Israel Noel, an old man living alone at Fayette, was found dead by neighbours in January 1901. His gold watch was missing and murder was suspected at first. The neighbours noticed freshly disturbed earth in his cellar, dug, and found the watch and $10,000 in gold. His son in the West was the heir. The find was reported across the county papers the same week. Pin is the village, not the house.
new.t: Recovered 1901; the lesson is the cellar. Find the Noel house on a c.1895-1900 Lafayette County plat or the 1900 census. Private land: ask first.
new.warn: Private land; the house lot is not yet found.
src: Vernon County Censor, 9 Jan 1901, p. 3, 'Hermit Leaves $10,000 Gold' (Newspapers.com 602637420)

src: Dunn County News, 30 Aug 1901, p. 3, 'Will of a Hermit' (Newspapers.com 542426699)
tw-parker-la-crosse-1901.st: The will gave $1,000 each to the YMCA and the La Crosse hospital, $3,000 to Thomas Shimmin and the rest to the First Baptist Church; a Brooklyn niece contested it for unsound mind and lost. No paper reports hidden money, a search or a find.
